channel.title: JUJU LipSync
channel.description: Updates for JUJU LipSync (direct download, beta).

item.title: Version 0.9.1 (2)
item.description:
JUJU LipSync 0.9.1

  • Renders finish about 10% sooner, with exactly the same picture: the model stays loaded between shots, the next shot is made ready while the current one is generated, and the shots that take longest to finish are made first.
  • The app reopens where you left it: the commercial, the render, the shot and the frame. Quit asks only while a render or an export is running.
  • Nothing is done twice: reopening a commercial reads back who is speaking instead of working it out again, and after you reassign a speaker only that shot is rendered again (Regenerate appears at once).
  • Finding the shots no longer depends on the graphics processor, and a picture that cannot be read is reported instead of opening as one shot.
  • If the Mac's graphics processor fails during a render, the shot says so and keeps the original.
  • Cancel stops everything, including an export. Go waits for the speaker analysis. Frame rates such as 29.97 stay frame-accurate.
  • A approves a shot and moves to the next one waiting; Shift-A approves all.
  • The source header is green and the master's red.
  • Switching to the original no longer jumps in level: at the speakers it is turned down to the master's loudness (Playback menu to turn this off). The master and everything you export are untouched.

item.title: Version 0.9.0 (1)
item.description:
JUJU LipSync 0.9.0 — first beta for invited testers

  • On first launch, Engine Setup builds the on-device engine on your Mac from its original sources, about 20 GB. Every file is checked before use, and if the install stops it carries on where it left off.
  • Drop the original commercial on the left and the commercial with the new dialogue on the right, then press Go.
  • Review shot by shot, approve, then export the master, a viewing copy and the dialogue report.
  • Updates arrive in the app: JUJU LipSync → Check for Updates….
  • Needs an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 26 or later, at least 32 GB of memory (64 GB or more recommended) and Homebrew.
